title: CI runner control profile: the validation and promotion lanes, the runner's placement and configuration, its reach to Gitea, the Gitea-side configuration and the governance workflow

decision.note: Hostile-CI threat model, the validation and promotion lanes, and the CI runner's reach to Gitea: the Architect's design, revision 2, accepted by the Overseer at Q-02.1's completion (rulings R1 and R2); every act it names stays Owner-gated.

statuses.decided: Decided by decision 0016 (Accepted); the leaf named in verify_at builds or proves it.
statuses.planned: A proposed value or step that the leaf named in verify_at fixes and proves.

acceptance.clause: No untrusted PR validation job has any necessary reason or configuration path to production/Owner credentials.
The CI runner's reachability to Gitea and the job token's use are decided against decision 0013 point 7.
Every forward is an Owner act.

lanes.name: Validation lane: the disposable job container
lanes.executes: Untrusted proposal content at an exact revision, cloned from a staged and verified bundle, after the governance workflow's first three steps.
lanes.produces: Log lines and a conclusion, streamed by the runner. No status, no artifact, no merge, no effect.

lanes.name: Validation lane: the CI guest and its runner
lanes.executes: act_runner (pinned at Q-02.2.1) and Moby, launching each job as a disposable container under the declared configuration.
lanes.produces: The run record's log and conclusion, over the runner RPC only.

lanes.name: Promotion lane (trusted)
lanes.executes: Staging the bundle, dispatching the governance workflow, reading the run record, posting aieh/validation, the protected merge (an Owner act), the independent verification and the privileged effects. No step of it is a Gitea Actions job on the validation runner; no Actions context ever holds a promotion credential.
lanes.holds: every credential mapped to trusted-lane in the token policy
lanes.produces: The required status context, the merge and any effect, each under Owner authorization.

shared_object: The exact revision: the proposal SHA and the sha256 of the bundle that carried it. The promotion lane reads Gitea's run record and never consumes a file a job wrote.

placement.runner: gitea-runner 6.0.0 (act_runner, renamed upstream), pinned at Q-02.2.1 in composition/lock/components.lock.json: the Linux amd64 release binary with its checksum; the job image docker.io/library/python:3.12-trixie by index, linux/amd64 manifest and image id (the Overseer's selection of 2026-11-12 under C-3).
placement.host: A dedicated disposable CI guest: a CI variant of profiles/strong-windows-qemu-whpx (same provider, accelerator, image, seed pattern, guards, lifecycle verbs and P1 to P12 contract), provisioned by the decision 0006 pattern with Moby, the runner and the job image, and without the Agent Server.

ceilings.notes: Confirmed by the Owner at C-3 on 2026-11-11: 4 vCPU, 6 GiB memory, 20 GiB system disk, 40 GiB working disk. The CI profile variant declares them.

lifetimes.detail: Reused for successive jobs within a session; recreated at every policy or pin revision, after any failed containment probe, when the runner is deleted and at least at each unit boundary; the runner is deleted at destroy.
One guest per validation; the runner record and its token die with the single task (G2).

lifetime_choice.notes: The Owner's C-3 answer of 2026-11-11: one guest reused within a validation session, with the disposable per-job containers, networks, storage isolation, disabled caches and mandatory recreation conditions of the shared lifetime; the guest is destroyed at the session's end, and a compromised or unverified guest is never reused. The runner registers without --ephemeral and is deleted at destroy.

placement.runner_user: A dedicated guest service user in the CI guest's docker group (root-equivalent inside the CI guest only); the agent login stays out of the docker group (P6).

label.name: aieh-validation
label.image_rule: the image id: docker://sha256:<the linux/amd64 config digest of the lock entry>; never a tag or a repository digest
label.notes: The Overseer's ruling C of 2026-11-12: decision 0006 item 3 loads images by docker load and checks that the image id equals the locked config digest; a loaded image may carry no repository digest in Moby's classic store, and the runner pulls an image its reference does not find (act/container/docker_images.go 19-42; docker_pull.go 33-47, 77-85), which decision 0016 T9 forbids. The label's argument after docker:// is the image reference (internal/pkg/labels/labels.go 30-50, 58-80). That the reference resolves to the loaded image is observed at Q-02.2.2.

rules.notes: The Overseer's ruling A of 2026-11-12 (the exchange mount): exactly the declared read-only sources (runner_config.volumes).
Empty: one network per job, behind the guards (br-+); never host.

Not a key at 6.0.0 (internal/pkg/config/config.go 176-194, 204-207); an unknown key only warns (config.go 291). The Overseer's ruling of 2026-11-12 on the C-3 record's findings (the IPv6 key): the rule follows container.network_create_options.enable_ipv6, and the stale key is declared nowhere.
Decision 0016 section 2.3 (container.enable_ipv6: false) at the 6.0.0 key (config.go 204-207; internal/app/run/runner.go 609-611); declared explicitly, not left to Docker's default.

The Overseer's ruling of 2026-11-12 on the C-3 record's findings (the unpinned keys): a key of the pinned 6.0.0 config the declaration must pin; decision 0016 sections 2.3 and 11. True mounts the workspace from a host directory and adds it to the valid volumes (act/runner/run_context.go 278-280; config.example.yaml 300-305).

The Overseer's ruling of 2026-11-12 on the C-3 record's findings (the unpinned keys): a key of the pinned 6.0.0 config the declaration must pin; decision 0016 sections 2.3 and 11. It acts on what a job creates through its Docker proxy, which docker_host "-" never gives a job (config.example.yaml 309-311).

The Overseer's ruling of 2026-11-12 on the C-3 record's findings (the unpinned keys): a key of the pinned 6.0.0 config the declaration must pin; decision 0016 sections 2.3 and 11. shared mounts one tool cache volume that successive jobs reuse: cross-job poisoning (config.go 196-202, 380-385; internal/app/run/runner.go 629-630).

The Overseer's ruling of 2026-11-12 on the C-3 record's findings (the unpinned keys): a key of the pinned 6.0.0 config the declaration must pin; decision 0016 sections 2.3 and 11. Hook scripts run inside the job before its first step and after its last (config.go 101-105; act/runner/job_hooks.go 29-35). Their ACTIONS_RUNNER_HOOK_JOB_* fallbacks are read from runner.envs and env_file, both empty (job_hooks.go 30, 34; docs/job-hooks.md line 17).

The Overseer's ruling of 2026-11-12 on the C-3 record's findings (the unpinned keys): a key of the pinned 6.0.0 config the declaration must pin; decision 0016 sections 2.3 and 11. A script run on the runner host after each task (config.go 94; internal/app/run/runner.go 310).

The Overseer's ruling of 2026-11-12 on the C-3 record's findings (the unpinned keys): a key of the pinned 6.0.0 config the declaration must pin; decision 0016 sections 2.3 and 11. Headers added to every runner request to Gitea, Register included (config.go 74; internal/app/cmd/register.go 346-353; daemon.go 180).

The Overseer's ruling of 2026-11-12 on the C-3 record's findings (the unpinned keys): a key of the pinned 6.0.0 config the declaration must pin; decision 0016 sections 2.3 and 11. A Prometheus listener of the runner (config.go 241-246; daemon.go 240).

The Overseer's ruling of 2026-11-12 on the C-3 record's findings (the unpinned keys): a key of the pinned 6.0.0 config the declaration must pin; decision 0016 sections 2.3 and 11. Opt-in task admission, with an optional script run on the runner host (config.go 248-256; internal/app/run/runner.go 813, 894).

options.notes: The option names are decided (decision 0016 section 2.3); the user id and the limits are fixed by the CI profile variant (Q-02.2.1). No mount is an option: at the 6.0.0 pin a bind given in container.options passes the valid-volume filter and is dropped while valid_volumes is empty (act/container/docker_run.go 653, 1126-1159), so the exchange moved to container.volumes (runner_config.volumes).

volumes.disclosure: At the 6.0.0 pin each container.volumes source is also admitted, read-only, as a source a workflow's own volumes may use (act/runner/run_context.go 284, 290-301; act/container/docker_run.go 1311-1331; the upstream test run_context_test.go 311-312), so a workflow could re-mount the same read-only exchange or wheel set at another target; no other host path and no write become reachable, which keeps T7 and T9. The governance workflow's checked rules (no container:, services: or uses:) leave the one workflow that runs unable to declare a volume.
volumes.notes: The Overseer's ruling A of 2026-11-12 (the exchange mount) and ruling D (the job's Python tools set): container.volumes holds exactly these read-only sources, valid_volumes stays empty. Each spec is appended verbatim to the job's binds, :ro kept (run_context.go 303-313; config.go 328-332); it also reaches service and Docker-action containers, which the governance workflow never declares.

environment.notes: The Overseer's ruling of 2026-11-12 on the C-3 record's findings (the runner environment): the runner process's environment is declared (the variant's service block: its environment and argv) and checked, names compared without case. GITEA_RUNNER_LABELS is the daemon's --labels default, which overrides the registered labels (internal/app/cmd/cmd.go 56); GITEA_RUNNER_REGISTRATION_TOKEN is the register token's environment path (register.go 88, 205-208); HTTP(S)_PROXY and NO_PROXY reach every job (internal/app/run/proxy.go 19-67; runner.go 508-509); DOCKER_HOST would replace the guest's own socket the runner finds (daemon.go 381-403); OTEL_* configures trace export (internal/pkg/telemetry/telemetry.go 66-91); ACTIONS_RUNNER_HOOK_* is refused as a stale form (the runner reads it from runner.envs only). config_expansion: ${NAME} in a config.yaml value is replaced from the runner's environment at load (config.go 510-531), so the declared config carries no $.

registration.performer: The host-side Gitea-administration command (the gitea_roles.py class), which holds the site-administrator credential; never the dispatcher or the CI guest.

procedure.detail: Reset the governance repository's registration token through the web settings route (POST /{owner}/{repo}/settings/actions/runners/reset_registration_token) under a site-administrator web session (the F-06.1 sign-in flow, with CSRF); every older token for the scope is invalidated.
Read the fresh token with gitea actions generate-runner-token --scope <org>/<repo> into memory, never to a log or file.
Hand it to the dispatcher in memory for one delivery over the management channel to the CI guest's provisioning step.

gitea-runner register --no-interactive --config <the declared config.yaml> --instance http://127.0.0.1:13300 --token-file <a root-only file on /run, removed after the call> in the CI guest: no --ephemeral in the shared lifetime chosen at C-3; the labels come from the config only. The guest keeps only the runner token.
Reset again immediately after a successful registration or a failed delivery: the delivered value is dead before any job runs.

token_input.notes: The Overseer's ruling of 2026-11-12 on the C-3 record's findings (the registration token): the registration token enters by file only, never the command line (--token, visible in the process list) or the environment (GITEA_RUNNER_REGISTRATION_TOKEN); the file lives on /run (tmpfs), root-only, and is removed after the call, so no registration token is at rest. At 6.0.0 --token-file takes precedence and its content is trimmed (internal/app/cmd/cmd.go 36-37; register.go 196-216); --config must be given, or register falls back to four default ubuntu labels (register.go 90-95, 304-313).

fallback.detail: Never in force for a live runner (the Owner's direction of 2026-11-10, decision 0016's dated note, point 1): a registration token that stays active between provisionings, read at each one and reset only on revision or exposure, is not admitted as a residual.

live_gate.rule: No live runner is registered or qualified until the reset is verified live to invalidate the delivered value: after the second reset, the delivered registration token is refused by Register (the negative probe).
alternatives: An ephemeral-runner design: one CI guest per validation, the runner record and its token dying with the single task (G2).
A reset performed as an Owner act.
live_gate.authority: The Owner's direction of 2026-11-10 (decision 0016, dated note, point 1; the Owner-action queue's OA-13 row): if the automated reset is unavailable or does not invalidate the value, Q-02.2.2 stops at this gate and presents an alternative.

every_other_repository.notes: Every repository that receives proposals (the integration repository, the fixture, any planning repository) has Actions disabled: a proposal's workflows never run, and no scoped workflow runs there either (G10).

live_check.performer: The host-side Gitea-administration command's --gitea mode, read-only: Gitea's database and the API as the site administrator (decision 0016 section 6.6). Not this checker's; never run by Q-02.1.
live_check.report_interface: tools/check_ci_policy.py --live-report FILE (an interface only until Q-02.3.1)

reach.path: The runner process to Gitea's runner RPC over the dispatcher-held remote forward bound to the CI guest's loopback (endpoint ci-control); never a job.
reach.basis: Decision 0013 point 7 stays as written: the runner is pinned upstream software operated by the harness in a contained domain, not untrusted code.

reach.path: A job reaches no Gitea, host, execution guest, resolver or internet: the egress guard (empty allowlist), the container guard, icc off, SLIRP restrict=on and the loopback-bound forward. GITHUB_SERVER_URL, GITHUB_API_URL and the runtime URLs inside a job name the container's own loopback.
reach.basis: Decision 0013 point 7: untrusted code has no network path to Gitea.

reach.path: The dispatcher stages the verified bundle into the CI guest's exchange over the existing management and exchange classes (loopback hostfwd).
The reporter (aieh-bot-ci) dispatches the governance workflow and posts aieh/validation over host loopback.
Gitea never connects to a runner or a job: the runner polls (G2).
The optional host-side filtering proxy on 127.0.0.1 as the forward's target (proxy).

endpoint.description: The CI runner's control channel to Gitea's runner RPC, reachable from the CI guest's own processes only, never from a job container.
endpoint.forward: ssh -N -R 127.0.0.1:13300:127.0.0.1:<target> held by the dispatcher inside the qualified management channel, with ExitOnForwardFailure=yes, keepalives, the per-instance key and the profile's client options
endpoint.lifetime: Only while a validation session is open; recorded beside the launch record (pid, bind, target, instance); re-established idempotently; the runner's poll fails closed while it is down.

p7_class.notes: Profiles P7 gains the class with the CI profile variant; Q-02.1 records it only.

proxy.adoption: Overseer ruling R1 (2026-11-10): the host-side filtering proxy is the planned target of the ci-control forward; owned code built at Q-02.2.1; its listener is Owner act A-4. If A-4 is refused, disclosure ci-d3 stands with Gitea's whole HTTP surface.
proxy.notes: The Overseer's ruling of 2026-11-12 on the C-3 record's findings (the job-summary post), disclosed: the runner itself posts each step's job summary to <ACTIONS_RUNTIME_URL>/_apis/pipelines/workflows/<run>/jobs/<job>/steps/ (under /api/actions_pipeline/) with the job's runtime token when Gitea advertises the capability (act/runner/job_executor.go 540-575). The proxy denies it; the upload is best effort and does not fail the job (job_executor.go 666), so job summaries are not available. Whether Gitea 28.3.0 advertises the capability is not read.

workflow.runtime_home: aieh-governance/quality-workflows, mirrored by the dispatcher's push to its protected default branch; the trusted lane records the commit and blob sha it dispatched.
workflow.dispatch: workflow_dispatch with ref the protected default branch and return_run_details=true, by aieh-bot-ci only.
workflow.allowed_repositories_note: Empty: every validation fails closed until a leaf adds a repository (the fixture at Q-02.2.2, the integration repository at its first real consumer).

approval.quote: Accept these ceilings for the dedicated CI guest:

owner_acts.notes: Answered 2026-11-11 (option 1): the ceilings, one guest reused within a validation session, destroyed at the session's end, never reused when compromised or unverified; it authorizes no live registration, Actions activation, guest network change, untrusted workload or other OA-13 act.

checks.what: No validation lane holds an owner, admin, executor or management credential; the job holds exactly the two task tokens and the runner host exactly the runner token; the profile's lanes equal the token policy's map.
Every inventory credential has exactly one lane, and a credential held in a CI domain is in that domain's lane.
The validation job reaches nothing, and every task token's reach is none and is never relied on.
Each task token row names an inventory credential of the validation job with a permissionless effective permission on the governance repository.

Every runner-configuration invariant is declared at its decided value, and a profile variant's declared config.yaml satisfies them and carries no environment expansion; the variant's runner service sets no forbidden environment variable and no label override.
Every workflow under policy/ci/workflows obeys decision 0016 section 7.3.
Actions is enabled on the governance repository only, no repository is public, and the governance protections are complete.
Restricted mode and an all-none ceiling at the governance owner and repository; no cross-repository grant anywhere.
No Actions secret or variable is allowed anywhere.
The filtering proxy admits exactly the runner RPC, Register only in the provisioning window.

The registration procedure resets the token before it is read and after registration; the fallback is never in force; a live runner waits on the live reset proof, and its absence blocks (Owner direction, 2026-11-10); the token enters by file only, and a variant's register call reads the declared config, names the ci-control instance and is ephemeral exactly when the chosen lifetime is per-validation.
Every Owner act names its requesting leaf, and an observed one cites its bootstrap-log approval verbatim.
Every forward and host listener names an Owner act.
A fact verified at source names its paths and lines in the archive the lock pins; a live one cites evidence; an unverified one names its leaf.
The revocation rows equal the role-token matrix's.
Every inventory, matrix, role, plan-leaf and decision id resolves, and every statement carries a status and a verify_at leaf.
No machine path appears; the README's block equals --render; this list names every code the checker emits.
